properties.name: model-cards:integration_means
properties.value: Hugging Face Transformers format weights compatible with vLLM, SGLang, TokenSpeed; deployable via SGLang, vLLM and TokenSpeed; usable through the Chat Completions API (OpenAI Python SDK) including Qwen Cloud; thinking mode required, with reasoning_effort (xhigh default, medium, low) and preserve_thinking options.

properties.name: model-cards:distribution_channels
properties.value: Open weights and configuration files in Hugging Face Transformers format (compatible with vLLM, SGLang, TokenSpeed); official Qwen API service via Qwen Cloud (Qwen3.8-Max); Qwen Studio chat app; deployable with SGLang, vLLM, TokenSpeed

modelParameters.architectureFamily: Causal Language Model with a hybrid Mixture-of-Experts architecture (Gated DeltaNet and Gated Attention layers, each followed by MoE); 2.4T total / 95B activated parameters
modelParameters.modelArchitecture: Causal language model with 2.4T total and 95B activated parameters; 92 layers; hidden layout 23 × (3 × (Gated DeltaNet → MoE) → 1 × (Gated Attention → MoE)); Mixture of Experts with 512 experts, 10 routed + 1 shared activated; hidden dimension 8192. Built on the architectural foundation of Qwen3.5. The card gives no detailed rationale for the design choices.

performanceMetrics.value: The card has a benchmark table with a Qwen3.8-Max column, covering coding agent, general agent and general capability benchmarks (for example GPQA Diamond 92.6). Terminal Bench 2.1 was evaluated with Claude Code (avg@10).

useCases: Designed for coding, professional work, research, and long-horizon agentic tasks, carrying complex multi-step tasks through to completion; text-only generation with thinking mode.
Agentic systems and coding/development tools: designed for long-horizon, multi-step agentic tasks, with support for popular harnesses and development tools for integration into existing stacks
technicalLimitations: No dedicated limitations section. The card notes that the model is text-only, with no multimodal input, and that thinking cannot be disabled. It also notes that a higher presence_penalty (used to reduce endless repetition) may occasionally cause language mixing and a slight decrease in model performance.

properties.name: model-cards:max_output_size
properties.value: Recommended maximum output length of 262,144 tokens for reasoning content and 131,072 tokens for the final response (within the 1M context length)

properties.name: model-cards:eval_methodology
properties.value: Benchmark footnotes give per-benchmark settings. Terminal Bench 2.1 was run with Claude Code (avg@10), a 5-hour timeout and max_tokens=131,072. SWE-bench Pro used the Claude Code harness, temp=1.0, top_p=0.95 and a 256K context window. QwenSWEBench used the Claude Code harness, avg@3, an 8-hour timeout, max_tokens=32,768, temperature=1.0 and a 256K-token context window.

properties.name: model-cards:autonomy
properties.value: The card describes autonomous agentic behaviour: stronger autonomous planning and handling of environment feedback, designed to carry complex multi-step tasks through to completion. It states no human-in-the-loop oversight requirement.

components.name: Evaluated on benchmarks including Terminal Bench 2.1, SWE-bench Pro, DeepSWE 1.1, NL2Repo-Bench, FrontierSWE, MLS-Bench-Lite, PaperBench, AndroidBench, SkillsBench v1.1, Automation-Bench, WideSearch, $OneMillion-Bench, PLawBench, plus in-house QwenSWEBench, QwenQoderBench, QwenReactBench, QwenSVGBench and CoWorkBench (the table also lists others, e.g. GPQA Diamond, HLE, IFBench, HealthBench, MRCR v2, LongBench v2).
